quests.protocolRule: What can you say confidently, and what can't you?
quests.crisisScene: A parent says her daughter texted from school, 'someone has a gun', with no other detail. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT SERIOUSLY WITH THE SCHOOL, THE TEXT, AND THAT DETAILS ARE UNCONFIRMED
quests.actionGuidance: A potential threat to many people needs a fast response, and the report should be clear that it's unconfirmed.

quests.protocolRule: Who has actually searched?
quests.crisisScene: School staff say they don't see anything unusual. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND POLICE TO VERIFY, NO VISIBLE SIGNS DOESN'T MEAN NO THREAT
quests.actionGuidance: Staff may not know what a student has hidden, so police should check.

quests.protocolRule: Would you want callers discouraged from reporting?
quests.crisisScene: Police confirm it was a toy in a student's bag and there's no threat. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ACKNOWLEDGE IT, CLOSE THE INCIDENT, AND NOTE THE REPORT WAS MADE IN GOOD FAITH
quests.actionGuidance: Good-faith reports should be encouraged even if the outcome is harmless.

quests.protocolRule: Can you confirm the source?
quests.crisisScene: A resident smells gas at a building's entrance. A neighbor says it's probably from the restaurant next door. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT AND KEEP PEOPLE AWAY FROM IGNITION SOURCES UNTIL CHECKED
quests.actionGuidance: A gas smell should be treated as a real hazard until the source is confirmed.

quests.protocolRule: Did the check rule out every source?
quests.crisisScene: The meter reader says the meter is fine, but the smell persists. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: STILL REPORT IT, THE LEAK MAY BE ELSEWHERE
quests.actionGuidance: A clear meter only rules out that source. A lasting smell needs further investigation.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Are you sure of the cause?
quests.crisisScene: The smell only seems to appear after someone runs the bathroom exhaust fan. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE PATTERN AND LET RESPONDERS IDENTIFY THE SOURCE
quests.actionGuidance: The pattern is a useful clue, but diagnosing it is for the responders.

quests.protocolRule: Which is easier to fake or misjudge: a label or a sweaty pallor?
quests.crisisScene: A woman says her husband has chest tightness. He says it's heartburn, but he's pale and sweaty. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: GO WITH THE OBSERVED SIGNS AND CALL FOR AN AMBULANCE
quests.actionGuidance: Pale, sweaty skin with chest tightness are objective warning signs that override his own guess.

quests.protocolRule: Is a refusal an end to the call?
quests.crisisScene: He refuses to go to the hospital. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: EXPLAIN THE RISK, KEEP THE CALL OPEN, AND LET PARAMEDICS ASSESS HIM
quests.actionGuidance: Paramedics can assess and explain, and the operator can stay on the line.

quests.protocolRule: Which extra details would change the urgency?
quests.crisisScene: A young man has sharp chest pain after a hard gym session. It's worse when pressing on his breastbone and his breathing is normal. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: ASK ABOUT OTHER SYMPTOMS AND ARRANGE PROMPT ASSESSMENT, ESCALATE IF BREATHLESS OR SWEATY
quests.actionGuidance: The pattern suggests muscle strain but can't be assumed. Extra warning signs would escalate it.

quests.protocolRule: Who has the more recent view?
quests.crisisScene: One witness says a suspect ran west, another says east. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT BOTH DIRECTIONS AND ASK WHICH WITNESS SAW HIM LAST
quests.actionGuidance: Recording both and identifying the latest sighting gives police a starting point.

quests.protocolRule: Which source is more reliable than memory?
quests.crisisScene: A store camera shows him getting into a car headed south. Input police code!
quests.optimalResponse: UPDATE POLICE WITH THE VERIFIED DIRECTION
quests.actionGuidance: Camera evidence can outweigh witnesses' recollection.

quests.protocolRule: Does rounding up help the police?
quests.crisisScene: A witness says she's 'almost sure' the car was blue. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT IT AS 'ALMOST SURE', NOT AS CERTAIN
quests.actionGuidance: Overstating certainty could send police after the wrong vehicle.

quests.protocolRule: Did the situation stay the same as at the start?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports her mother has stomach pain. During the call she becomes pale, sweaty, and drowsy. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL THE OPERATOR IT'S GETTING WORSE AND REQUEST HIGHER URGENCY
quests.actionGuidance: Worsening during the call means the initial urgency no longer fits.

quests.protocolRule: Is this something to save for later?
quests.crisisScene: The mother vomits blood. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE BLOOD IMMEDIATELY
quests.actionGuidance: Vomiting blood suggests serious internal bleeding and must be relayed immediately.

quests.protocolRule: What did the earlier signs suggest?
quests.crisisScene: The daughter says she thinks her mother ate old food and feels better now. Input medical code!
quests.optimalResponse: LET PARAMEDICS DECIDE, DON'T CANCEL ON A GUESS
quests.actionGuidance: A feeling of improvement doesn't cancel the earlier warning signs.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: What details can you give without getting close?
quests.crisisScene: A driver passes a leaking truck with a hazard placard but can't read the number. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE PLACARD'S COLOR AND SHAPE AND WHAT YOU SEE FROM A SAFE DISTANCE
quests.actionGuidance: Even partial placard information helps responders identify the hazard class.

quests.protocolRule: What's the cost of a mistake here?
quests.crisisScene: He asks whether to move closer to read the number. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: NO, STAY BACK, AN INCOMPLETE REPORT IS SAFER THAN A RISKY ONE
quests.actionGuidance: Responders can identify the substance properly. Getting closer risks exposure.

quests.protocolRule: What can a photo add?
quests.crisisScene: Another driver zooms a photo from far away. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SHARE THE PHOTO WITH RESPONDERS IF THEY CAN USE IT
quests.actionGuidance: A zoomed photo may capture placard details the callers couldn't read.

quests.protocolRule: Can you keep people in while investigating?
quests.crisisScene: Students in a classroom complain of headaches and a strange smell. The teacher can't find a source. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: MOVE EVERYONE OUT AND REPORT THE SYMPTOMS AND THE SMELL
quests.actionGuidance: Removing people from a possible exposure protects them while the source is identified.

quests.protocolRule: What does spreading suggest?
quests.crisisScene: Another classroom in the same corridor reports similar symptoms. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THAT MORE ROOMS ARE AFFECTED, SUGGESTING A BUILDING-WIDE SOURCE
quests.actionGuidance: More rooms affected points to a shared source, such as ventilation.

quests.protocolRule: Is a plausible cause proven?
quests.crisisScene: A custodian says he used a strong cleaner in the corridor earlier. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TELL RESPONDERS ABOUT THE CLEANER, IT MAY BE THE SOURCE BUT LET THEM CONFIRM
quests.actionGuidance: It's a useful clue, but only responders can confirm whether it explains the symptoms.

quests.protocolRule: Where can a small child be in danger within seconds?
quests.crisisScene: A mother says her four-year-old went to the yard 'a minute ago' and can't be found. The yard has a gate and a pool. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CALL FOR HELP AND CHECK THE POOL AND WATER FIRST
quests.actionGuidance: Water is the fastest danger for a toddler, so it's checked first while help is called.

quests.protocolRule: What does an open gate change?
quests.crisisScene: The gate is open. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: REPORT THE OPEN GATE AND ASK RESPONDERS TO SEARCH THE STREET TOO
quests.actionGuidance: An open gate means the child may have left the property, so the search area is larger.

quests.protocolRule: Has anyone actually seen the child?
quests.crisisScene: A neighbor calls to say the child is with her and safe. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: CONFIRM THE CHILD IS THERE AND SAFE BEFORE TELLING RESPONDERS
quests.actionGuidance: Confirming the child in person prevents a false stand-down.

quests.protocolRule: Which call risks a life right now?
quests.crisisScene: During a storm, calls report downed trees, blackouts, flooding, and one person trapped in a car in floodwater. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: PRIORITIZE THE TRAPPED PERSON, THEN OTHER LIFE-THREATENING HAZARDS
quests.actionGuidance: A person trapped in rising water is the most time-critical.

quests.concept: On-Scene Evacuation Prior to Unit Arrival
quests.protocolRule: Is anyone in immediate danger?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a tree on a road, and no one is hurt. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: LOG IT AS A NON-URGENT HAZARD
quests.actionGuidance: With no injuries, it's a hazard for road crews rather than an urgent emergency.

quests.protocolRule: Who is near it?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a sparking transformer next to a bus stop with people waiting. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: TREAT IT AS URGENT, A LIVE ELECTRICAL HAZARD NEAR PEOPLE
quests.actionGuidance: Sparking electrical equipment near people is a serious hazard.

quests.protocolRule: What if he's not asleep?
quests.crisisScene: A caller reports a man lying in a parking lot, maybe sleeping. A guard says he moved a little earlier. It's raining and cold. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: SEND HELP TO CHECK HIM, THE UNCERTAINTY IS ITSELF THE RISK
quests.actionGuidance: The cold and uncertain condition make a check the safest choice.

quests.protocolRule: Which parts are facts, and which are guesses?
quests.crisisScene: Paramedics arrive. He's conscious but disoriented and cold. He says he took medication earlier. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: RELAY WHAT HE SAID ABOUT THE MEDICATION EXACTLY WITHOUT ADDING GUESSES
quests.actionGuidance: The exact statement helps paramedics, and guesses could mislead them.

quests.protocolRule: Could labeling affect his care?
quests.crisisScene: The guard wants to tell them the man 'is probably an addict'. Input code!
quests.optimalResponse: STICK TO OBSERVATIONS, NOT ASSUMPTIONS ABOUT THE PERSON
quests.actionGuidance: Assumptions can bias care. Observations help paramedics assess him.
